saw.short: Hunger Games film pops up in US election coverage
saw.headline: The Hunger Games *crashes the US midterms* coverage
saw.what: Viewers spotted an in-universe President Snow video airing during US midterm election coverage, indy100 reports. It showed “Please Standby” and “Break the machine”, with Maya Hawke’s Mags saying “All machines can be broken”, then a 10-second countdown. The film, Sunrise on the Reaping, opens on 20 Nov (UK date to be confirmed).
saw.why: A film stunt dropped into a moment everyone was already watching. A neat template for Hexed.

saw.short: KFC UK launches a Marvel Doom menu
saw.headline: KFC goes *full Doctor Doom* with a black-bun burger
saw.what: KFC’s first Marvel tie-up, for Avengers: Doomsday, includes a black sesame bun Doom Burger with Smoky Green Mayo, Doom Dripped Wings and a Doom Shake. It starts 9 Nov and, Dexerto reports, runs in the UK until January 2027, with items varying by market. The film opens 18 Dec.
saw.why: Film marketing through food. A close comparison for any Disney cinema push.

saw.headline: Arsenal *beat Slavia Prague 2‑1* in the Champions League
saw.what: Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored before Wiktor Nowak pulled one back late on, per Metro. Ezri Konsa went off with a knee problem and William Saliba was on the bench for the first time this season. Arsenal host Hull City on Saturday.
saw.why: Midweek football gives a big shared conversation. Single source for now.

saw.headline: Greggs’ *begging turkeys* split customers
saw.what: Greggs’ Christmas windows show cartoon turkeys begging to be let in, beside lines like “All taste, no turkey”. Some customers said the posters made the Festive Bake seem meat-free. This year’s bake is chicken, ham hock and bacon. Metro reports the ASA has received complaints but opened no investigation.
saw.why: Humour that confuses people. A lesson in checking a joke can’t be misread.

saw.short: Strictly's Jaime Winstone misses Saturday's show
saw.headline: Strictly’s *Jaime Winstone* will miss Saturday
saw.what: Jaime Winstone is out of Saturday’s show after doctors advised rest for a torn abdominal muscle. Metro reports she and partner Carlos Gu go through to next week. Her statement says: “I am in considerable pain”.
saw.why: Strictly news travels fast on a Thursday. Fans will talk about it all week.

saw.short: Fans link Andrew Garfield's GQ shoot to American Psycho
saw.headline: Fans think *Andrew Garfield’s GQ shoot* is an American Psycho tease
saw.what: Fans online are speculating, with no casting confirmed, that Garfield’s GQ shoot nods to American Psycho. Metro says it features pinstripe suits and a black latex-look coat. Director Luca Guadagnino has only said “Maybe one day I would do” it.
saw.why: A fan theory with zero confirmation. Interesting for how images get read as clues.

platform.short: Snap hits 495m daily users, no growth in Europe
platform.headline: Snap hits *495m daily users*, but not in Europe
platform.what: Snap says it had 495 million daily active users in Q3, up from 493 million in Q2, with no growth in North America or Europe. Revenue rose 14% year on year to $1.72bn, according to Social Media Today. Snap’s own release wasn’t checked.
platform.why: Growth is coming from outside our markets. UK reach is flat.

platform.short: LinkedIn adds a Post Performance Table
platform.headline: LinkedIn adds a *Post Performance Table*
platform.what: LinkedIn has added a table showing impressions, views and watch time for each post in one place. Social Media Today also lists new metrics for saves and sends, and in-network versus out-of-network views. Rollout timing wasn’t given.
platform.why: Easier post-by-post reporting for anyone running LinkedIn.
